Subject: Next steps: RapidOnramp evaluation milestones and SDK routing map

Hi Samir & Lisa —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and a proposed, pragmatic evaluation plan so we can align owners and timelines. I kept this intentionally lightweight so the team can execute quickly.

Goal for the evaluation
- Validate Redwood powers your onramp flows with <100ms token latency for interactive paths and acceptable cost at expected QPS.
- Confirm integration surface (SDK + API) and tool-calling path for the retrieval/LLM orchestration you sketched.

Success criteria (we agreed these on the call)
1) Feature: End-to-end flow that returns structured intent + entity extraction with ≥95% accuracy on the three test scenarios you supplied.
2) Latency: median per-token generation latency <= 120ms on the demo dataset; p95 <= 300ms for streaming endpoints.
3) Stability: no more than two transient errors per 10k requests during a 1-week soak.
4) Cost: projected per-1k-token cost within the budget band you set (Samir: goal = <$0.80 per 1k tokens for the primary route).
5) Security: confirmation of acceptable data retention window (see Samir's note below) + receipt of SOC2 summary and data processing terms.

Proposed timeline (tight, 4 weeks total):
- Tech spike (this week): Redwood provides SDK snippets + streaming demo; Rapid Onramp runs initial connect tests (3 business days).
- Integration sprint (weeks 1–2): implement SDK routes, wire tool-calling for retrieval augmentation, and iterate on prompt templates.
- Soak & metrics (week 3): run the 1-week soak with telemetry collection.
- Review and go/no-go (end of week 4).

Owners (to confirm)
- Rapid Onramp: Samir (POC lead), Mike (eng lead, infra/latency owner).
- Redwood: Sergio (sales/coordination), Dev Patel (integration engineer), Marissa Cole (CS & success metrics), Laura Bennett (instrumentation/telemetry).

Integration notes (high level)
- SDK: recommend Node + Python SDKs for the PoC; we'll attach a minimal Node snippet (sdk-snippet-node.txt).
- API routes: /v1/generate for batch, /v1/stream for real-time. Streaming supports SSE and websockets; we'll default to SSE for browser flows and websocket for low-latency backend streams.
- Tool calling: Redwood supports structured function/tool calling (json schema). For retrieval augmentation, call the retrieval tool first and pass the top-K documents into the model via the tools interface.
- KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching on repeated session tokens to reduce cost for warm sessions.

Attachments: RapidOnramp-MVP-checklist.xlsx (MVP acceptance table), sdk-snippet-node.txt (minimal bootstrap).

Next steps
1) Samir/Mike: confirm owners and PII retention window by EOD Thu (30 Sep).
2) Dev/Marissa: we'll ship the snippets and a telemetry checklist by EOD tomorrow.
3) Schedule a 30-min integration kickoff — propose Mon 4 Oct @ 11:00 PT.

Looking forward — happy to adjust timeline if you need more runway.

—
Sergio Alvarez

Sergio — thanks for the clear summary. Quick confirmations and one ask from security so we can unblock legal.

Confirmed
- Owners: Samir (POC), Mike (eng).
- Timeline: the tight 4-week cadence works for us if the tech spike is immediate.

Security ask
- Can Redwood share a SOC2 Type II summary or an attestation doc we can share with procurement? We need this to begin our internal approval fast path.
- Data retention: we need the ability to set a 30-day retention window for session content + an option for immediate delete on demand for dev/test data. Is that supported?

Success metrics tweak
- For the accuracy metric, can we add a secondary threshold for intent classification (≥97% on the primary intent class)? That will be our gating criterion for the next phase.

Thanks — if those are doable we'll lock in Mon 4 Oct for the kickoff.

Thanks — a few quick technical clarifications and recommended defaults for the PoC implementation.

1) Streaming vs batch
- For your interactive onramp flows we recommend using /v1/stream (SSE) for browser clients and a websocket bridge for your backend orchestration where you need sub-100ms token latency end-to-end. SSE is simpler to implement for demos; websocket gives slightly lower end-to-end latency but requires a persistent connection.

2) SDK usage
- Use the Node SDK for your backend service that proxies requests to Redwood. Example (attached sdk-snippet-node.txt) shows the minimal flow: authenticate via API key (vault this), open stream, hydrate the KV cache for session warm starts.

3) Function/tool calling
- We'll use the tools API to pass retrieval results as structured arguments. Example flow:
  * Retrieval service returns top-5 docs (id, score, snippet)
  * Call the tool "retriever" that returns structured JSON which the model can then reference in generation via tool outputs.

4) Telemetry and instrumentation
- We'll provide a telemetry checklist (CSV row per KPI) and recommended event names: request.start, request.end, token.generated, model.error, cache.hit. We'll push a template to the Drive folder (link below).

5) Compliance note (Samir's request)
- We support configurable retention windows per tenant and a manual purge API for test datasets. I'll attach the SOC2 summary to the Drive folder and loop in Security for any additional docs you need.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRapidOnrampTech
Internal docs (streaming & SDK): https://redwood-internal.company/docs/sdk/streaming
